To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the essential TRAPP complex component Trs20p has a role in endocytic trafficking in addition to its previously known roles in anterograde trafficking and autophagy.
the yeast TRAPP complex subunit Trs20 is required for sporulation and endocytic recycling.
the essential TRAPP subunit Trs20 plays a critical role in endocytic trafficking and sporulation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the yeast TRAPP subunit Trs20 in endocytic trafficking, sporulation and meiosis.
understanding the role of Trp20 in membrane trafficking in yeast and its role in sporulation.
understanding the function of TRAPP complexes in membrane trafficking and the role of Trp20 in these processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the role of Tr20p is not in anterograde trafficking but in recycling endosomes and meiosis.
the Trs20p mutants have no defects in anterograde trafficking but have defects in endocytosis and sporulation/meiosis.
Trs20p plays a role in endocytic trafficking and in meiosis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Trs20 is essential and mutations in Trs20p affect the function of TRAPP in different membrane trafficking pathways and in sporulation.

Trs20p has an essential role in the function of all TRAPP complexes, but that the role of Trp20p in the TRAPP complex involved in ER-to-Golfi transport is distinct from that in the TRAPP complexes involved in post-Golgi transport or in autophagy.
Trs20p plays a role in endocytic trafficking and sporulation, which are likely to be mediated by the post-Golgi/endosome-to-Golgi TRAPP complex.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Trs20p has a role in endocytic trafficking, and that the role of TrAPP complexes in anterograde trafficking may be redundant.
TRAPP complexes are likely to play a role in endocytic trafficking and that Trs20p has a specific role in the meiotic process.
the role of Trp20p in the TRAPP complex is not essential for general anterograde trafficking but is important for endosomal recycling and meiosis.
